exercises.english: The repair can be done in ten minutes.
exercises.german: Diese Reparatur lässt sich in zehn Minuten erledigen.
exercises.why: sich lassen expresses possibility; the verb stays an infinitive with no zu, and the subject of sich is the thing itself.

exercises.english: The application form can be filled in online.
exercises.german: Das Antragsformular lässt sich bequem online ausfüllen.
exercises.why: The form is the reflexive subject and ausfüllen is a separable infinitive, so the prefix joins it: ausfüllen, not aus zu füllen.

exercises.english: A mistake like that cannot be undone.
exercises.german: Ein solches Versehen lässt sich leider nicht wiedergutmachen.
exercises.why: wiedergutmachen is inseparable, so the prefix sits inside the infinitive; leider carries the speaker's assessment.

exercises.english: An appointment can only be made by phone.
exercises.german: Der Termin lässt sich nur telefonisch vereinbaren.
exercises.why: Only narrows the possible method; the agent is irrelevant, which is exactly what sich lassen leaves out.

exercises.english: There is no way to avoid the fee.
exercises.german: Die Gebühr lässt sich nicht umgehen.
exercises.why: umgehen is inseparable and um- is a stressed prefix, so the word keeps its form inside the infinitive.

exercises.english: The vegetables freeze very well.
exercises.german: Das Gemüse lässt sich gut einfrieren.
exercises.why: Object-as-subject plus einfrieren; separable ein- attaches directly to the infinitive.

exercises.english: The car can hardly be sold any more.
exercises.german: Der Wagen lässt sich kaum noch verkaufen.
exercises.why: kaum noch doubles the restriction and keeps the focus on the difficulty rather than on a seller.

exercises.english: This task can also be solved without previous knowledge.
exercises.german: Diese Aufgabe lässt sich auch ohne Vorkenntnisse lösen.
exercises.why: The bare infinitive lösen follows the reflexive pronoun; a zu would be wrong here.

exercises.english: The new rules can no longer be changed.
exercises.german: Die neuen Regeln lassen sich nicht mehr ändern.
exercises.why: nicht mehr marks a change that has already become final, which suits the impersonal evaluation of sich lassen.

exercises.english: The obstacle could only be overcome with great difficulty.
exercises.german: Das Hindernis ließ sich nur schwer überwinden.
exercises.why: Präteritum of lassen (ließ) with a bare infinitive; lassen changes its stem vowel in the past.

exercises.english: The fridge is easy to clean.
exercises.german: Der Kühlschrank lässt sich leicht reinigen.
exercises.why: reinigen is separable, so the prefix is glued to the infinitive; leicht replaces a free would-expression.

exercises.english: The offer can hardly be beaten.
exercises.german: Das Angebot lässt sich kaum noch unterbieten.
exercises.why: unterbieten is inseparable and keeps the prefix ui-; the sense of to beat on price is expressed by the infinitive.

exercises.english: It is not easy to find a car park here.
exercises.german: Hier lässt sich kaum ein Parkplatz finden.
exercises.why: With dative objects sich lassen takes zu plus infinitive, and the order is zu before the separable verb.

exercises.english: The software can be downloaded for free.
exercises.german: Die Software lässt sich kostenlos herunterladen.
exercises.why: herunterladen is separable, so the prefix attaches to the infinitive; kostenlos names the condition, not an agent.

exercises.english: This material can be recycled easily.
exercises.german: Das Material lässt sich leicht recyceln.
exercises.why: recyceln is a bare infinitive with no prefix and no zu, the simplest sich lassen pattern.

exercises.english: The results cannot be clarified by phone.
exercises.german: Die Ergebnisse lassen sich nicht telefonisch klären.
exercises.why: klären is a weak separable verb, so the prefix moves to the end of the infinitive phrase: klären.

exercises.english: The contract can be cancelled at any time.
exercises.german: Der Vertrag lässt sich jederzeit kündigen.
exercises.why: kündigen is separable with a umlaut; jederzeit makes the possibility unlimited in time.

exercises.english: This rule cannot sensibly be applied to cryptocurrencies.
exercises.german: Diese Regel lässt sich nicht sinnvoll auf Kryptowährungen anwenden.
exercises.why: The dative object Kryptowährungen forces the zu-infinitive: anzuwenden, with zu directly on the verb.

exercises.english: The error could be eliminated by restarting.
exercises.german: Der Fehler ließ sich durch einen Neustart beheben.
exercises.why: A past sich lassen with a means phrase introduced by durch plus accusative instead of a named agent.

exercises.english: Luckily the situation could be defused.
exercises.german: Die Situation ließ sich zum Glück entschärfen.
exercises.why: zum Glück as an adverbial before the infinitive shows the result-oriented, agentless reading.

exercises.english: I got the letter yesterday.
exercises.german: Ich habe gestern den Brief bekommen.
exercises.why: In the bekommen-passive the recipient is the subject and keeps the active accusative object.

exercises.english: She got her car back.
exercises.german: Sie hat ihr Auto zurückbekommen.
exercises.why: zurück is written as one word with bekommen; the reflexive-looking dative object Auto shows who benefits.

exercises.english: We got the application submitted.
exercises.german: Wir haben den Antrag eingereicht bekommen.
exercises.why: Perfect with two participles: the state (eingereicht) plus bekommen, which makes the recipients the grammatical subject.

exercises.english: He got his passport renewed.
exercises.german: Er hat seinen Pass erneuert bekommen.
exercises.why: The same double-participle pattern as with Antrag, but the accusative object is a person-related possessive object.

exercises.english: I got two tickets.
exercises.german: Ich habe zwei Karten bekommen.
exercises.why: Simple bekommen with an accusative object; nothing here is passive in the strict sense, yet the focus is on receiving.

exercises.english: They had their luggage delivered yesterday.
exercises.german: Sie haben ihr Gepäck gestern zugestellt bekommen.
exercises.why: bekommen + Partizip II: the recipient stays the subject, so this is not a passive.

exercises.english: She got an extension from the authority.
exercises.german: Sie hat von der Behörde einen Aufschub bekommen.
exercises.why: bekommen + Partizip II with the source expressed as a von-phrase, which would be a dative in the passive.

exercises.english: I got a new job.
exercises.german: Ich habe eine neue Stelle bekommen.
exercises.why: Stelle rather than Job, as in standard B2 usage; bekommen highlights the benefit for the subject.

exercises.english: He got a formal warning.
exercises.german: Er hat eine Abmahnung bekommen.
exercises.why: An unwelcome result still fits bekommen because the recipient is the subject, not the cause.

exercises.english: My aunt gave me the book.
exercises.german: Ich habe das Buch von meiner Tante bekommen.
exercises.why: The giver is expressed as a source with von plus dative after the past participle, not as a subject.

exercises.english: She got the news from her colleague.
exercises.german: Sie hat die Nachricht von ihrer Kollegin bekommen.
exercises.why: von plus dative marks the source; the dative ending -in on Kollegin is the standard female form.

exercises.english: We got permission from the landlord.
exercises.german: Wir haben die Erlaubnis vom Vermieter bekommen.
exercises.why: Vom is the contracted form of von dem, common with institutional sources in a bekommen-construction.

exercises.english: Did you get an answer?
exercises.german: Hast du eine Antwort bekommen?
exercises.why: A yes-no question with the separable prefix of bekommen in the first position of the main clause.

exercises.english: The mechanic gave me an explanation.
exercises.german: Ich habe von dem Mechaniker eine Erklärung bekommen.
exercises.why: With a source phrase plus object, the von-phrase can come first; it still leaves the recipient as subject.

exercises.english: Have you received the documents?
exercises.german: Haben Sie die Unterlagen bekommen?
exercises.why: Formal Sie as the subject of a bekommen-perfect question, the same form the active werden would require.

exercises.english: She got a lot of gifts for her birthday.
exercises.german: Sie hat viele Geschenke zu ihrem Geburtstag bekommen.
exercises.why: zu plus dative gives the occasion; the accusative plural object precedes the past participle.

exercises.english: He got the parcel.
exercises.german: Er hat die Sendung bekommen.
exercises.why: Sendung rather than Paket keeps the register neutral; bekommen covers a purely factual receipt.

exercises.english: I got an extension of the deadline.
exercises.german: Ich habe eine Fristverlängerung bekommen.
exercises.why: The long compound noun is the accusative object; the benefit-for-the-subject reading motivates bekommen.

exercises.english: He got a parking ticket.
exercises.german: Er hat ein Knöllchen bekommen.
exercises.why: A negative result is still expressed with bekommen, because the point is the effect on the subject, not the issuing authority.

exercises.english: We got a discount.
exercises.german: Wir haben einen Rabatt bekommen.
exercises.why: A modest benefit where bekäme would be less idiomatic; bekommen is the neutral everyday verb.

exercises.english: There is no smoking here.
exercises.german: Hier wird nicht geraucht.
exercises.why: The agentless passive: wird plus Partizip II with no subject, which is typical of a posted rule.

exercises.english: You have to park here.
exercises.german: Hier muss geparkt werden.
exercises.why: Modal plus passive: the modal is conjugated in the finite slot, geparkt then wird as an infinitive block.

exercises.english: In Germany you drive on the right.
exercises.german: In Deutschland wird rechts gefahren.
exercises.why: A general rule takes agentless passive; fahren keeps its stem change to the participle gefahren.

exercises.english: No work is done at the weekend.
exercises.german: Am Wochenende wird nicht gearbeitet.
exercises.why: Unpersönliches Passiv: no subject and no agent, the missing doer is left to be understood.

exercises.english: A lot of trees have been planted here.
exercises.german: Hier wurden viele Bäume gepflanzt.
exercises.why: Präteritum of the agentless passive, normal in German narrative prose rather than a Perfekt with many trees.

exercises.english: In that house, baking used to take place every morning.
exercises.german: In dem Haus wurde früher jeden Morgen gebacken.
exercises.why: Unpersönliches Passiv in the simple past with a time adverb in position I.

exercises.english: You can see the castle from here.
exercises.german: Von hier aus kann man die Burg sehen.
exercises.why: Here the impersonal passive is replaced by man, which points to any unspecified viewer rather than naming one.

exercises.english: One has to be patient.
exercises.german: Man muss Geduld haben.
exercises.why: A general recommendation with man as subject; the perfect-like idiom haben keeps the impersonal colour.

exercises.english: The causes are still being argued about.
exercises.german: Über die Ursachen wird noch gestritten.
exercises.why: Unpersönliches Passiv with an über-phrase and an agentless participle clause.

exercises.english: Tomorrow the results will be announced.
exercises.german: Morgen werden die Ergebnisse bekanntgegeben.
exercises.why: Future passive with werden in the finite slot; bekanntgeben forms one word with the participle bekanntgegeben.

exercises.english: From May the new software will be worked with.
exercises.german: Ab Mai wird mit der neuen Software gearbeitet.
exercises.why: Unpersönliches Passiv: gearbeitet takes the preposition mit, which governs the dative, so the noun phrase is der neuen Software.

exercises.english: People often complain about it.
exercises.german: Es wird oft darüber geklagt.
exercises.why: An impersonal passive with a prepositional object: the prefix of the participle attaches inside geklagt.

exercises.english: One should have read the contract.
exercises.german: Man hätte den Vertrag lesen sollen.
exercises.why: The Konjunktiv II of sollen with an infinitive at the end, giving a reproach without naming anyone.

exercises.english: Milk and cheese are sold in this shop.
exercises.german: In diesem Laden werden Milch und Käse verkauft.
exercises.why: The agentless passive with two subjects; the shop is only a place, not the doer, so it takes in plus accusative.

exercises.english: In the past many people were displaced.
exercises.german: In der Vergangenheit wurden viele Menschen vertrieben.
exercises.why: Past passive; vertreiben takes no ge- between prefix and stem in the participle.

exercises.english: That cannot be seen.
exercises.german: Das kann man nicht sehen.
exercises.why: man replaces the would-be agent, so the sentence is not a full passive but a man-impersonal one.

exercises.english: After dinner the table is cleared.
exercises.german: Nach dem Essen wird der Tisch abgeräumt.
exercises.why: A routine in the present passive; abräumen is separable, so the participle is abgeräumt.

exercises.english: It was reported that the accident had caused a jam.
exercises.german: Es wurde berichtet, dass der Unfall einen Stau verursacht hatte.
exercises.why: Two tenses in one sentence: reported in the preterite passive, the cause in the plusquamperfekt with verb last.

exercises.english: Smoking is not allowed in the rooms.
exercises.german: In den Räumen darf nicht geraucht werden.
exercises.why: Unpersönliches Passiv with a modal finite verb: modal first, participle, werden last.

exercises.english: The building is being renovated at the moment.
exercises.german: Es wird gerade renoviert.
exercises.why: A progressive passive without a stated agent; the word gerade marks the ongoing action.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: What is there to eat?
exercises.german: Was gibt es zu essen?
exercises.why: The classic es gibt plus zu-infinitive question, with essen unchanged after zu.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is a lot to do.
exercises.german: Es gibt viel zu tun.
exercises.why: The idiomatic impersonal alternative to a passive; the infinitive tun follows zu directly.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is a lot of room for improvement in this text.
exercises.german: In diesem Text gibt es viel zu verbessern.
exercises.why: Improvement is expressed as a zu-infinitive after es gibt, with no agent at all.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: What is there to report?
exercises.german: Was gibt es zu melden?
exercises.why: The melden counterpart of essen, showing that the es gibt frame takes many different infinitives.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: A lot still needs to be done.
exercises.german: Es muss noch viel getan werden.
exercises.why: muss with a passive infinitive in the es muss zu frame, keeping the agent out of view.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: The topic still needs to be discussed in more detail.
exercises.german: Das Thema muss noch ausführlicher besprochen werden.
exercises.why: Adverbial before the participle; besprechen is inseparable, so the participle is besprochen.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is nothing to object to.
exercises.german: Es gibt nichts zu beanstanden.
exercises.why: Nichts after es gibt plus a zu-infinitive, a fixed pattern in written reviews.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: What do we need to take into account?
exercises.german: Was ist bei der Anmeldung noch zu beachten?
exercises.why: The frame es ist plus zu plus infinitive turns the passive into a short impersonal question.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is a lot for which we have to thank her.
exercises.german: Es gibt viel, wofür man ihr danken muss.
exercises.why: The frame es ist plus zu plus infinitive replaces a passive with an unnamed person responsible.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is nothing more to do today.
exercises.german: Heute gibt es nichts mehr zu tun.
exercises.why: nichts mehr and nicht mehr both appear; the frame with tun is the everyday neutral wording.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is something to tidy up in the corridor.
exercises.german: Im Flur gibt es etwas aufzuräumen.
exercises.why: A separable verb in the zu-infinitive: the prefix goes inside, aufzuräumen.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is something to bear in mind here.
exercises.german: Hier gibt es etwas zu beachten.
exercises.why: beachten is a plain infinitive, showing that the zu frame accepts non-separable verbs unchanged.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: This proposal has to be revised.
exercises.german: Dieser Vorschlag muss noch überarbeitet werden.
exercises.why: A modal plus überarbeitet plus werden, the impersonal equivalent of a passive with an unnamed reviser.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is still a few things to do.
exercises.german: Da gibt es noch einiges zu erledigen.
exercises.why: Einiges as a partitive quantity, which cannot stand as the subject of a passive but fits es gibt perfectly.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: The decision must be made today.
exercises.german: Die Entscheidung muss heute getroffen werden.
exercises.why: treffen is inseparable and takes no ge- in the participle; the decision, not the decider, is the subject.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is not much to lose.
exercises.german: Es gibt nicht viel zu verlieren.
exercises.why: verlieren is inseparable, so the zu-infinitive is zu verlieren with the prefix inside the verb.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: This question still has to be clarified.
exercises.german: Diese Frage muss noch geklärt werden.
exercises.why: The klären-construction with muss and werden, the counterpart of es gibt etwas zu klären.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: There is a lot to improve in the planning.
exercises.german: Bei der Planung gibt es viel zu verbessern.
exercises.why: The zu-infinitive after es gibt expresses a deficiency in the planning, not an action by a named person.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: Do you have anything to declare?
exercises.german: Haben Sie etwas zu verzollen?
exercises.why: The customs formula keeps the same zu-infinitive frame; verzollen has a z-vowel change, not zzolln.

exercises.skill: es gibt / es muss + zu + infinitive
exercises.english: Two points still have to be clarified.
exercises.german: Zwei Punkte müssen noch geklärt werden.
exercises.why: A plural subject in a modal passive; Punkte needs no article change beyond the accusative zero ending.

exercises.english: The owner had the broken window replaced.
exercises.german: Die Eigentümerin ließ das kaputte Fenster ersetzen.
exercises.why: Because the same person arranges and benefits, the causative lassen plus infinitive is the right choice, not bekommen.

exercises.english: The landlord had the heating fixed.
exercises.german: Der Vermieter ließ die Heizung reparieren.
exercises.why: Causative lassen: the subject is the one who commissions, so it stays a subject of the lassen clause.

exercises.english: I had my hair cut.
exercises.german: Ich habe mir die Haare schneiden lassen.
exercises.why: The dative of advantage mir with a body part; the perfect is possible here, though the present is more common.

exercises.english: We had the flat renovated.
exercises.german: Wir haben die Wohnung renovieren lassen.
exercises.why: An external firm does the work, so lassen rather than bekommen, and the accusative object stays with the commissioning subject.

exercises.english: She had her car serviced.
exercises.german: Sie hat ihr Auto warten lassen.
exercises.why: warten lassen is inseparable, so no zu appears even after haben; ihr Auto is the dative object of advantage.

exercises.english: They had the leak repaired.
exercises.german: Sie haben das Leck reparieren lassen.
exercises.why: A separable infinitive after lassen: the prefix joins reparieren, and the agent is the plumber, not they.

exercises.english: The city had the road resurfaced.
exercises.german: Die Stadt hat die Straße neu asphaltieren lassen.
exercises.why: An institution commissioning work takes the lassen-construction with an infinitive, not a passive with von der Stadt.

exercises.english: The publisher had the manuscript proofread.
exercises.german: Der Verlag hat das Manuskript lektorieren lassen.
exercises.why: lektorieren is the industry term, and lassen plus infinitive expresses that the publisher arranged the check.

exercises.english: The office is being renovated at the moment.
exercises.german: Im Moment wird das Büro renoviert.
exercises.why: A neutral statement of a current fact: the agentless passive is right, while lassen would wrongly make the office the commissioner.

exercises.english: You are not allowed to smoke in this workshop.
exercises.german: In dieser Werkstatt darf nicht geraucht werden.
exercises.why: A prohibition needs the modal passive with werden; a man-clause would soften it into a personal remark.

exercises.english: You can buy the tickets at the counter.
exercises.german: Man kann die Karten am Schalter kaufen.
exercises.why: Possibility for any person is expressed with man and a modal, which sounds far better than a passive here.

exercises.english: A lot has been abolished since the reform.
exercises.german: Seit der Reform wurde vieles abgeschafft.
exercises.why: Vieles is a partitive subject that cannot become a normal passive subject, so the impersonal preterite passive is used.

exercises.english: What still has to be clarified in the contract?
exercises.german: Was muss im Vertrag noch geklärt werden?
exercises.why: The question is about the task, not about who does it, so a modal passive with an implicit es is the natural choice.

exercises.english: The participant was given a certificate.
exercises.german: Die Teilnehmerin hat ein Zertifikat bekommen.
exercises.why: bekommen-passive because the point is what the person received; a von-passive would be formal and unnecessary.

exercises.english: I received an unexpected invitation.
exercises.german: Ich habe eine unerwartete Einladung bekommen.
exercises.why: A simple receipt with a benefit for the subject, which is exactly the core meaning of bekommen plus Partizip II.

exercises.english: The question of financing still has to be clarified.
exercises.german: Die Finanzierungsfrage ist noch zu klären.
exercises.why: The short sein plus zu-infinitive variant, more compact than a modal passive in a written text.

exercises.english: The whole file can be scanned quite easily.
exercises.german: Die ganze Akte lässt sich gut einscannen.
exercises.why: A possibility, so sich lassen with the bare infinitive einscannen beats a Vorgangspassiv with a made-up agent.

exercises.english: The flat was cleaned before the viewing.
exercises.german: Die Wohnung wurde vor der Besichtigung gereinigt.
exercises.why: A completed past event with a time phrase: the normal Vorgangspassiv is the most natural here, agent dropped.

exercises.english: The package was sent by the student union.
exercises.german: Das Paket wurde von der Studentenvereinigung geschickt.
exercises.why: Here the agent matters for the fact, so it is kept as a von-phrase, which is possible in a Vorgangspassiv.

exercises.english: Our application was not accepted.
exercises.german: Unser Antrag wurde nicht angenommen.
exercises.why: The outcome is what matters, not who rejected it, so the agentless passive in the preterite is the right option.
